items.rationale: Necessary dismantling and refitting for access or drying is covered under §§5.2.6–5.2.7 if not already included in the dryer charge. One service is estimated at €90 gross, in line with Case 46.
Section 5.2.7 covers the necessary drying period supported by moisture readings. The claim describes about two weeks of drying, but this line bills only seven days, estimated at 7 × €42 = €294 gross.
Section 7.4.4 bars an unexplained surcharge without an itemised material list. The €36 conditional estimate uses Case 46 and would apply only if necessary materials were substantiated.

Sections 5.2.6 and 7.14(c) allow reinstatement of disturbed pipe insulation with a standard mineral-wool shell of the original diameter. One short section is estimated at €26 gross, consistent with Case 46.
Under §5.2.2, disposal of insured debris is paid once, based on actual volume. This is the first-listed charge for the shared disposal, estimated at €60 gross using Case 46.
Levelling the affected substrate is covered making good under §§5.2.6 and 7.1.5. One lot of standard levelling material is estimated at €36 gross using Case 46.

Section 5.2.6 covers necessary substrate preparation, but §§3.5(d) and 7.4.1 bar charging again for removal, levelling or labour billed elsewhere. If this is distinct work, 2.78 m² at about €30 per m² gives €83 gross.
Section 5.2.6 expressly covers a necessary service opening to reach or make good the damaged pipe area. One opening is estimated at €19 gross using the comparable drilling line in Case 46.
The tiles are within the §7.14(d) format limit; §§3.5(a) and 7.1.6 restrict pricing to standard grade. Five tiles cover 4.05 m² including cutting allowance, at about €40 per m² gross.

These tiles exceed the 90 × 90 cm threshold in §7.14(d), triggering §3.5(f)'s no-partial-payment rule; the line also overlaps the standard tile allowance. The €162 conditional figure represents standard tiles for the same repair, not the designer order.
Section 7.14(a) permits standard sanitary silicone for necessary reinstatement joints. At €12 per linear metre, 3.6 metres comes to about €43 gross, consistent with Case 46.
Section 7.4.2 permits the first travel charge per contractor per document. The single tiling travel line is estimated at €83 gross using Case 46.
Section 7.4.1 allows necessary hours at the customary trade rate, excluding labour already billed in other lines. Case 46 supports 14 hours × €90 gross = €1,260 for distinct reinstatement labour.

items.description: Remove basement drywall and insulation wool
items.rationale: Section 5.2.6 covers dismantling within the documented damage area, subject to substantiation of the flat rate under §7.4.4 and no duplicate disposal. Case 46 supports about €50 for drywall removal plus €40 for stripping insulation, excluding waste haulage.
Sections 5.2.6 and 7.1.5 cover removal of affected plaster only within the cellar damage area. Using Case 46 as a benchmark, about 2.8 m² at €28 per m² gives €78 gross.
Section 3.5(b) excludes work outside the documented damage area, and the claim identifies the attic work as unrelated. The €80 conditional figure is a benchmark for a small plaster removal job only.
Sections 3.5(d) and 5.2.2 bar the second charge for the same disposal already listed at item 5. The €60 conditional benchmark would apply only if this were established as the first eligible charge.
